target_customer: Software engineering teams that need fine grained, relationship based access control in their applications
problem: Teams hand build authorization logic that becomes brittle as products grow. Warrant offered a centralized, open source service modeled on Google's Zanzibar system.
business_model: Open source core with a hosted usage based cloud service

founders.name: Aditya Kajla
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page.

founders.name: Karan Kajla
founders.background_notes: Brother or relative relationship not stated in sources read.

technical_complexity.rationale: A low latency, globally consistent relationship based authorization engine modeled on Zanzibar is hard distributed systems work for a team of three.

defensibility.rationale: Authorization sits deep in an application's data model so switching is costly, but open source rivals such as SpiceDB and OpenFGA appeared and the core was itself open source.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: WorkOS acquired the team and product in April 2024 and relaunched it as WorkOS FGA. The open source repo stayed under Apache 2.0.

market_need_then: Google published the Zanzibar paper in 2019 and developers wanted an accessible implementation. The founders said no publicly available implementation existed when they started.

branding.domain_note: Used warrant.dev, a developer TLD domain, rather than the .com. A different company later used the name Warrant for marketing compliance at hellowarrant.com.

identity.logo: Wide primary wordmark hosted at warrant.dev

rebrands.why: Folded into the acquirer's product line after acquisition

branding.community_and_virality: Launch HN post and an open source repo with a developer blog on dev.to.

brand_strength.rationale: Developer community presence through open source and Launch HN, but a generic legal word shared with other companies, and the brand was absorbed within three years.

outcome_analysis: Warrant built an open source Zanzibar inspired authorization service that a three person team shipped in 2021, then sold the company and product to WorkOS in April 2024, where it became WorkOS FGA. Funding found was minimal and unverified, and competing open source engines from Auth0 and AuthZed emerged, so the exit looks like a strategic tuck in rather than a venture scale outcome. Terms were not disclosed.
notes: CB Insights lists a seed of about 130 thousand dollars dated 2021-09 with Y Combinator as investor, a single aggregator figure, so unverified and not recorded as a round. The WorkOS announcement page itself returned only a blog index on fetch, the April 23 2024 date comes from search results describing that post. Competitor search found Zanzibar style projects (SpiceDB, OpenFGA, Permify) without 2021 dated sources, so the list is empty. A different company named Warrant (marketing compliance) shares the name and was excluded.
